guard_streams.source: Automatic compensation: What you need to know

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the automatic-compensation guide on 20 July 2026.
Signed-up providers pay compensation automatically for qualifying broadband and landline failures.
A delayed repair after two full working days attracts £10.34 for each calendar day the service remains unrepaired.
A missed engineer appointment attracts £32.31 compensation.
A delayed start of a new service attracts £6.46 for each calendar day of delay.

guard_streams.source: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the social-tariff guide on 22 June 2026.
Social tariffs are available to households receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit and certain other benefits.
Ofcom states that current social-tariff prices range from £10 to £24.
Most listed tariffs provide unlimited broadband at speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
The guide says customers can generally switch to, leave, and remain on a social tariff without fees or mid-contract price rises.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband-switching guide on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new provider and that provider arranges the switch.
The old broadband service ends automatically once the new service is working.
Ofcom states that loss of service during a switch must not last longer than one working day.
Customers have a 14-calendar-day right to cancel a new broadband order.

guard_streams.source: Broadband complaints fall to record low

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q1 2026 complaints update on 23 July 2026.
The latest complaints figures cover January to March 2026.
Broadband complaints fell to six per 100,000 customers, compared with a peak of 40 per 100,000 in 2011.
TalkTalk generated the most broadband complaints, while Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest.
Collective complaints about major landline, broadband, mobile and pay-TV providers decreased from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026.

guard_streams.source: Making a complaint and using ADR schemes

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the ADR guidance on 5 May 2026.
Communications providers must maintain an accessible complaints code setting out contacts, investigation steps and timeframes.
ADR schemes independently assess complaints and are free for eligible customers to use.
A complaint can go to ADR after six weeks unresolved or earlier when the provider issues a deadlock letter.
Ofcom approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman as the two telecoms ADR schemes.
